title: Prove it is gone
brief:
The cart holds a **Blue Top** and a **Men Tshirt**. Remove the Blue Top and prove it left.

1. click the **X** next to the Blue Top — it is a link, and its accessible name is `Remove Blue Top`
2. assert its row (`#product-1`) is no longer visible
3. assert the table is down to **1** row

Removal takes 300 ms, so the row is still there the instant after you click. Negative assertions retry as well: they wait for the thing to *go away*.
starter:
from playwright.sync_api import Page, expect


def test_removing_a_product_takes_it_out_of_the_cart(page: Page):
    page.goto("https://automationexercise.com/view_cart")

    # Sanity check: we start with two rows.
    rows = page.locator("#cart_info_table tbody tr")
    expect(rows).to_have_count(2)

    # 1. remove the Blue Top

    # 2. its row should disappear

    # 3. one row should be left
solution:
from playwright.sync_api import Page, expect


def test_removing_a_product_takes_it_out_of_the_cart(page: Page):
    page.goto("https://automationexercise.com/view_cart")

    rows = page.locator("#cart_info_table tbody tr")
    expect(rows).to_have_count(2)

    page.get_by_role("link", name="Remove Blue Top").click()

    expect(page.locator("#product-1")).not_to_be_visible()
    expect(rows).to_have_count(1)

checks.label: One product is left in the cart
checks.feedback: The cart does not hold exactly one product. Did the X get clicked - and did your test wait the 300 ms for the removal to land?

checks.label: It is the Blue Top that went, not the other one
checks.feedback: The wrong product was removed. Each X has its own accessible name: "Remove Blue Top" and "Remove Men Tshirt".

checks.name: not_to_be_visible
checks.label: You assert the row is gone with not_to_be_visible()
checks.feedback: No negative visibility check ran. expect(page.locator("#product-1")).not_to_be_visible() waits for the row to disappear - a plain `assert not ....is_visible()` would check too early and pass for the wrong reason.

checks.name: to_have_count
checks.label: You check the row count before and after
checks.feedback: I only saw one to_have_count. Keep the starting check as well - it proves the test began from the state you thought it did, so a later failure means something real.

hints.label: Nudge
hints.text: The X links have aria-labels, so get_by_role("link", name="Remove Blue Top") finds exactly the right one without any CSS.

hints.label: Strategy
hints.text: expect(page.locator("#product-1")).not_to_be_visible() for the row, then expect(rows).to_have_count(1) - you can reuse the `rows` locator from the top, because a locator is only an address.

reveal:
Two things worth keeping.

**Negative assertions wait too.** `not_to_be_visible()` retried for the 300 ms the removal took. `assert not row.is_visible()` would have passed instantly - and would also have passed if you had clicked the wrong button entirely, because the row would still be there but the assertion would have looked before the page moved.

**Assert your starting state.** The `to_have_count(2)` at the top costs one line and turns "the test failed" into "the test failed *after* the setup was correct".
